2024 - 2025 · Sole Technical Writer / Migration Lead

Documentation Platform Migration

Led the end-to-end migration of docs.swimlane.com from MadCap Flare to Archbee, reducing costs by ~80% while improving search, AI-assisted discovery, and content modularity.

Platform MigrationCost OptimizationContent ArchitectureArchbeeMadCap Flare

Problem

The documentation platform for a security automation product was running on MadCap Flare, a legacy desktop-based authoring tool. This created several compounding problems:

  • High annual licensing cost ($26,000+/year) with limited collaboration capabilities
  • No native search quality or AI-assisted discovery for customers
  • Content was tightly coupled to the tool, making modular reuse difficult
  • Publishing workflows were manual and error-prone during product releases
  • Support and field teams struggled to find answers quickly, increasing escalation load

My Role

As the sole technical writer, I owned the entire migration end-to-end: platform evaluation, content conversion, restructuring, parallel release support during the transition, and production rollout validation.

What I Did

  1. Evaluated and selected Archbee as the target platform based on cost, API capabilities, search quality, and content modularity
  2. Converted all content from MadCap Flare output to Archbee-compatible Markdown, including restructuring navigation and information architecture
  3. Cleaned up legacy content by removing outdated material, consolidating duplicate topics, and improving task-based organization
  4. Maintained parallel release support throughout the migration, ensuring no release shipped without documentation coverage
  5. Conducted two months of platform validation before production rollout, testing search accuracy, rendering, navigation, and cross-linking
  6. Coordinated production cutover with minimal disruption to customers and internal teams

Constraints

  • Single-person documentation team with no migration budget for contractors
  • Active product releases continued throughout migration (no content freeze)
  • Legacy content had inconsistent structure, requiring manual cleanup during conversion
  • Platform readiness had to be validated against customer-facing usage patterns, not just internal testing

Outcomes

Customer Impact

  • Improved self-service with faster search and Ask AI capabilities
  • Better content discoverability through task-based reorganization aligned to user workflows
  • Support and field teams reported faster answer discovery, reducing escalation dependency
  • Leadership and peer recognition described the new experience as "game changing"

Business Impact

  • Reduced annual platform cost from $26,064 to $5,592 (~80% reduction)
  • Year-one savings of $17,672 after accounting for migration effort
  • Enabled modular, reusable content architecture for future scalability
  • Zero documentation gaps during release cycles throughout the transition

Lessons Learned

  • Parallel release coverage is non-negotiable during a migration; content freezes are rarely possible in enterprise products
  • Two months of pre-production validation was critical; issues that appear minor in staging (broken cross-links, rendering differences) become customer-facing problems at scale
  • Cost savings alone do not sell a migration internally; the improved customer experience (search, AI, modularity) is what gets leadership support
